title: Constrained Non-negative Matrix Factorization for Guided Topic Modeling of Minority Topics
task: Discovering low-prevalence (minority) topics such as mental-health discussion
problem: Topic models miss low-prevalence themes; guided models need topic-specific seeds and over-fit to them.
architecture: NMF minimising generalised KL divergence with inequality constraints: documents without seed words cannot have high minority-topic prevalence (on W) and minority topics must carry some seed-word mass (on H); one domain seed list, no per-topic seeds; KKT conditions give new multiplicative updates with Lagrange multipliers.

datasets.name: Finnish YouTube data
datasets.details: 5,578,289 raw comments from 20 YouTubers; 2,979,969 after filtering; average 7.04 words

datasets.name: Synthetic
datasets.details: 500 documents with injected words from 18 mental-health topics

key_results: Synthetic data (20 topics, 7 minority): Purity 0.1765 and NMI 0.2453 vs best baselines 0.0969 (NMF) and 0.2247 (GuidedNMF).
Mean JSD 0.53783, close to KeyATM (0.53462) and NMF (0.54451).
strengths: Needs only one seed list for the whole domain and still splits it into data-driven subtopics.
Large real-world case study on non-English (Finnish) social media.

limitations.text: Evaluating low-frequency topics is hard; real data has no annotated minority topics, so quantitative results are on synthetic data only.
Absolute purity values are low for all models (best 0.1765); KeyATM has a slightly lower mean JSD.
